runs.prompt:
The corpus argument is exactly ky. Answer the following maintainer question with evidence from the frozen ky repository. Choose your searches and what to read; you may search again or batch needed reads. Cite file and line(s). Keep the answer to the question asked. Use only text_search, text_read as evidence; no other tools, files, web, tests or edits. Starting symbol: mergeHeaders.
How does Ky decide whether the user supplied Content-Type, and what header inputs does it consult for that decision? Cite the implementation, including the exact predicate.
runs.answer_summary:
Ky decides whether the user supplied a Content-Type by checking only the `options.headers` argument passed to the constructor, normalized through `mergeHeaders({}, options.headers).has('content-type')`. A `Request` input's own headers are excluded, because the constructor merges them into `this.#options.headers` first. The flag gates two behaviors: the automatic `application/json` header for `json` bodies, and deletion of the inherited Content-Type when a `Request` input is rebuilt with a FormData or URLSearchParams body.

Predicate (source/core/Ky.ts:524-525):
```ts
// A `Request` input's headers are already merged in, so only a content-type from `options.headers` counts as user-provided.
const userProvidedContentType = options.headers !== undefined && mergeHeaders({}, options.headers).has('content-type');
```

Inputs consulted:
- `options.headers` (the constructor's options argument, not `this.#options.headers`). When it is `undefined`, the predicate is `false`.
- The `Request` input's headers are not consulted. They are merged into `this.#options.headers` at Ky.ts:486 (`mergeHeaders((input as Request).headers, options.headers)`), which is why the raw `options.headers` is read instead.

Normalization (source/utils/merge.ts:73-86): `mergeHeaders` copies the base source into a new `Headers`, then applies each entry of the second source. A value of `undefined` (or the string `'undefined'` in a `Headers` instance) is a deletion marker and calls `.delete`. `Headers.has` is case-insensitive, so `Content-Type` and `content-type` both match.

Uses of the flag:
- Ky.ts:527-532: when `json` is set, `body` is stringified and `content-type: application/json` is set only if `!userProvidedContentType`.
- Ky.ts:536-542: when `input` is a `Request` and the body is `FormData` or `URLSearchParams`, the inherited `content-type` is deleted (so `Request` regenerates it with the boundary) only if `!userProvidedContentType`.

Lines 527-532: JSON content-type default gated by the flag. Lines 536-542: Request-input content-type deletion gated by the flag.
Lines 73-86: `mergeHeaders`, which builds a fresh Headers from source1 and applies source2 entries, treating `undefined` values as deletions.
Lines 191, 1457, 1514: documented behavior that a caller's `headers` Content-Type takes precedence over the automatic JSON and FormData types.

args.i: Reading mergeHeaders and content-type decision code

runs.prompt:
The corpus argument is exactly ky. Answer the following maintainer question with evidence from the frozen ky repository. Choose your searches and what to read; you may search again or batch needed reads. Cite file and line(s). Keep the answer to the question asked. Use only text_search, text_read as evidence; no other tools, files, web, tests or edits. Starting symbol: mergeHeaders.
How does Ky decide whether the user supplied Content-Type, and what header inputs does it consult for that decision? Cite the implementation, including the exact predicate.
runs.answer_summary: Ky decides whether the user supplied Content-Type with one predicate, computed once in the Ky constructor from the per-call `options.headers` only. It does not consult the Request input's headers, the merged `#options.headers`, or hooks. Predicate (source/core/Ky.ts:524-525): `const userProvidedContentType = options.headers !== undefined && mergeHeaders({}, options.headers).has('content-type');`. It is true only when `options.headers` is defined and its normalized header map contains `content-type` (Headers.has is case-insensitive). `mergeHeaders` (source/utils/merge.ts:73-86) builds a fresh Headers from the second argument and deletes keys whose value is `undefined`, so `{'content-type': undefined}` counts as not supplied. `toHeaderObject` (merge.ts:170) normalizes the input first; for a Headers instance the string 'undefined' is a deletion marker. The predicate gates two behaviors: (1) when `json` is set, `application/json` is written only if `!userProvidedContentType` (Ky.ts:527-531); (2) when the input is a Request and the body is FormData or URLSearchParams, the inherited content-type is deleted so Request regenerates it with the correct boundary, only if `!userProvidedContentType` (Ky.ts:536-542). The merged headers are built at Ky.ts:486 as `mergeHeaders((input as Request).headers, options.headers)`, which is why the comment at Ky.ts:524 excludes Request-input headers from the predicate. Docs agree that an explicit headers content-type always wins (readme.md:191, readme.md:1457, source/types/options.ts:51). Relevant tests: test/headers.ts:887-897, test/headers.ts:911-920, test/request-construction.ts:299-323. Not verified: how an init hook that sets content-type interacts with this predicate. test/hooks.ts:6960-6966 suggests the hook value wins, but I did not trace the code that produces that result.

`mergeHeaders` at lines 73-86 (undefined values delete keys); `toHeaderObject` at line 170 (Headers 'undefined' string as deletion marker); `mergeHeaderContainers` at line 188.
`KyHeadersInit` type at line 39; `headers` option at line 502; json docs stating explicit Content-Type takes precedence at line 51.
Docs for precedence of explicit Content-Type: line 191 (json), line 1457 (FormData), line 1514 (custom Content-Type).
Tests at 887-897 (json replaces Request-input content-type) and 911-920 (undefined removes automatic content-type).
Tests at 299-323 for URLSearchParams replacing a Request content-type and an explicit header kept for FormData on a Request input.

runs.answer_summary: Ky decides "user supplied Content-Type" with one predicate in the Ky constructor: `options.headers !== undefined && mergeHeaders({}, options.headers).has('content-type')` (source/core/Ky.ts:525). citations.description: Defines the predicate: `const userProvidedContentType = options.headers !== undefined && mergeHeaders({}, options.headers).has('content-type');`, preceded by the comment "A `Request` input's headers are already merged in, so only a content-type from `options.headers` counts as user-provided." `options` is the constructor parameter, after init hooks ran in `Ky.create`.

citations.path: source/core/Ky.ts (Ky constructor, same block, line numbers not returned by graph)
citations.description: Consumers of the flag: (1) `if (this.#options.json !== undefined) { ... if (!userProvidedContentType) this.#options.headers.set('content-type', 'application/json'); }`; (2) when `input` is a `Request` and the body is FormData or URLSearchParams and `!userProvidedContentType`, it calls `this.#options.headers.delete('content-type')` so the native Request sets the multipart boundary.

`mergeHeaders(source1, source2)`: copies source1 into a `new Headers(...)`, then for each entry of `toHeaderObject(source2)` deletes the key when the value is `undefined`, otherwise sets it. Called as `mergeHeaders({}, options.headers)` for the predicate, so only `options.headers` is evaluated; a `content-type: undefined` entry yields false.
